639.saw: Handwritten English despatch about the Carreras, Lima, Buenos Aires and Monte Video with numeric code passages interlined in the text: runs of 3-4 digit numbers (about 200-1500) separated by commas, nine or more runs across both pages, no decipherment written on the page. Date of the letter not legible at this resolution; text concerns the Carreras (Jose Miguel Carrera, president of Chile) and the Portuguese troops.
639.note: Matches the frame given in the entry (naId 213803757).

641.saw: Anderson's despatch No. 7 of 19 Jan 1824 is on this roll; the enclosed paper is on frames 0055-0058: handwritten Spanish letter, headed on 0057 'Al Sr. Ministro de Estado y Relaciones Exteriores de Colombia', with long runs of cipher (continuous loop/stroke characters, no word breaks) between clear Spanish phrases; 0055 and 0056 are mostly cipher with clear sentences interspersed; 0058 has a continuation plus an interleaved English 'Translation' sheet addressed to the Minister of State and foreign relations of Colombia, partly blank where the cipher lies. Not read.
641.note: Frames 0055-0058 of T33 roll 3, not roll 2 (roll 2 ends with Todd's despatch of 28 Jan 1824).

654.saw: Typed German telegram copies headed 'deutsche gesandtschaft sthlm' / 'legation allemande sthlm': 1256 is a long telegram of 4-5-digit groups (017 732 405 135 ...) in about 28 lines ending 'hintze'; 1257 has 5-digit groups plus a few clear words ('funfacht vanadopote'), about 8 lines; roll 114 frame 0416 has a further 4-digit telegram ending 'stumm'. No decipherment on the pages.
654.note: The first named frame (roll 141 1255, roll 114 0415) is the covering Stockholm despatch (nos. 1426 / 1421, enclosing copies of German telegrams): no cipher there; the cipher starts on the next frame.

669.saw: Typed copy of a radiogram 'From Moscow to Stockholm', 21 March 1921, Delsovpra Kerzhentsev, Sirius, about 11 lines of five-digit groups (30215 82750 15123 ...), operator note 'Two or three groups missing owing to interference', signed Tchicherine. No decipherment. Frame 0871 (Bristol No. 153, 20 Apr 1921) also seen: letter text with the operator's notes, no cipher.

675.saw: MID name-index card: entry 'Re ltr. fr M. Lop... to --- written in code which --- could not decipher. States it may have been intended for Gustav Moller, Ger. Consul stationed at Guaymas, Mex.', file 8-II, DJ 5/20/18. Index card only; no cipher text.

676.saw: MID cross-reference card 'SUSPECT. WELCH, F. P., Apartado No. 10, San Luis Potosi': 10632-27, Postal Censor Jan 26-18, letter to his wife enclosing a message which he could not decipher; Heraldo of Mexico pro-German. Index card only; no cipher text.
676.note: Card names the writer as F. P. Welch.

677.saw: MID record card PF-10570, subject MINUTH, Fred R. (Grand Haven, Mich.): item 2, 17 May 1918 memo from Col. Pakenham: active authoritative German agent corresp. in cypher via Sweden and Switzerland with Berlin, Swiss intermediary St. Gall. Index card only; no cipher text.
677.note: Card names the subject as Fred R. Minuth.

678.saw: Typed sheet headed 'Agents. For Bohemia / Armenian / English' with runs of line/letter fraction groups (4/3 - 1/14 3/4 5/5 4/7 ... 10/5 10/7 9/7 8/3 8/4 8/6 ...), about 9 lines, followed by 'Decode: (1) ... Racine, Wis. (2) Milwaukee ... (4) Peter Barry, 48 Milwaukee St.' (Bureau decode of four addresses). More fraction runs on PDF page 14 (by OCR text) and p. 939.
678.note: The cipher is in the 940A PDF (1000 pp); the 940C PDF had no matching text and 940B was not examined.

693.saw: G-2 report 7190 / MA Riga report 6943, 12 Oct 1928, English text with Russian five-figure groups: 0431 has the 4 Aug 1928 message (about 45 five-digit groups, key 'mep', call signs zit/bup) and a 10 Aug message (about 10 groups, key 'big'); 0432 has the 24 Aug message (11 groups, key 'dub', Avrora). No decipherment, only the attache's comments.
693.note: Keys per the page: 4 Aug 'mep'; 10 Aug 'big'; 24 Aug 'dub'. The entry's '4 Aug, key big' appears to be the 10 Aug message.

694.frame: M1194 roll 91 frame 0195; M1085 roll 760 frame 0286
694.saw: 0195 is the MID cross-reference card for GUPTA, Haramba Lal: line '10020-87, C,MIS Nov.7-17, Cipher letter of Prince ---'; no cipher text. M1085-760-0286 (printed 'German Plots and Intrigues' p. 52, scanned upside down) quotes the Gupta cipher-message extract of 16 Nov 1916 and the telegram 'not as yet satisfactorily deciphered' in substance (decipherment, not ciphertext); no cipher groups.

703.saw: Typed letter 24 Mar 1917, Barnes to H. B. Hook, Nogales: Weiskopf says it is almost impossible to decode the 'Unger code message' to the Swiss Consul, San Francisco; asks for more messages. No cipher text on it. Frames 2024-2025 and 2027-2030 also looked at: Bureau reports and letters, no cipher.
703.note: Message text not located in frames 2024-2030.

705.saw: 364: typed copies of Vigo-consul telegrams of 12.11.1939 with time stamps: 5-digit numeric groups (13778 15336 ...) mixed with letter-group lines (eltib prucj ishgz ...), about 40 lines, no clear text. 362-363 (Marineattache Madrid B.Nr. 128/39, 20.11.39) are covering letters, 365 a Verfuegung, 366 a different letter. Roll 2866: 504 five-digit Gibraltar telegram with German note; 508 handwritten 5-digit groups 'Gibraltar - H.B.M. Consul Las Palmas'.

706.saw: 505: 14 five-letter groups (NAUII ICMQO ...) '1800/22/4 Agente Consulaire France' with German informant note; 506: 'Nota - Num, 3', 24 five-letter groups, '1930/24/24 - Agente consulire France', German note. Frame 507 not viewed. No decipherment.

707.saw: Radio-Telegramm forms (DEBEG), no clear text: 877 taken 3.8.1940 10.30 GMT, DGR-DZG DFB-DFQ, heading '10 90 2 2113 = nairl errjw ...', about 150 five-letter groups in 12 lines; 878 taken 1.8.1940, '9 28 30 1701 - zgrwa ...', about 35 groups. Stamped 'IV 2311/40 gKdos'.

709.saw: US Army Field Message No. 5, Vladimirovka 9 July 1919, to Commanding General Amex Force, Vladivostok: 32 five-letter groups in 4 lines (LJEQE WJJOM RFAHN OVLBO ... XXKOX XALYX), 'Given to Japanese Captain 7/8/19 to be sent to Vladivostok by wireless', signed Williams. No decipherment.

720.saw: Typed DOJ record slip 9-16-12-3169-9, W SC 4-12-18: 'Atty. Encloses copy of code message found upon person of Edmond DeSalm Horstmar. Obrian Bielaski.' Slip only; no cipher text.

757.saw: 0113: 'Sent February 18 1918', to 'Naval Commander San Francisco', 17 five-letter groups in 3 lines (FVFRO TFKFX JTQII ...), signed American Consul General. 0114: '(COPY) Received March 1, 1918', Washington DC via Pacific, 'usgovt', 37 words: 31 ten-letter lowercase groups in 8 lines (Ssblnodyym dncrvjjwij ...) plus a final 'yrjmp 17527'. No decipherment.
757.note: Outgoing cable is 17 groups (c. 85 letters), not the c. 20 groups / 98 letters in the entry.

758.saw: 0505: copy no. 35 of telegram Musquiz 25 June 1906, Guajardo to Governor Cardenas, Saltillo: English text with two-digit code numbers (88 80 18 99 ... 30 83 98 10) and a few 'le 11' items interspersed with clear words, about 20 lines, no decipherment. 0514: Root's telegram of 14 Nov 1907 ('Mexican Embassy ... unable to decipher it'), no cipher.
758.note: Clear passages on this copy are already in English; the code numbers stand for words.

680.saw: NARA catalogue (proxy API) lists all three series at series level with zero digital objects; no frames to open.
